name: TX-25
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Roger Williams holds a massive financial edge, raising about $1.6 million against roughly $5,000 for Dione Sims
Sims reports negative cash on hand, indicating little to no active general-election campaign
The district's R+11 lean and incumbency strongly favor Republicans
Prediction markets price Democratic winning chances near 2%, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an R+11 district, a multi-term incumbent with a seven-figure war chest, a challenger who has raised almost nothing and sits in the red, and markets giving Democrats about a 2% chance. With no polling to the contrary, this is effectively a Safe Republican hold.
model.watch: Any late infusion of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected poll showing a single-digit race would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 25th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Roger Williams enters the general election with every structural advantage. The district's partisan lean sits near R+11, and Williams, a multi-term incumbent, has raised about $1.6 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand. Democratic nominee Dione Sims has raised roughly $5,000 and reports negative cash on hand, pointing to a campaign with little visible infrastructure or spending capacity.

No public polling covers the race and no national ratings agencies have weighed in, but prediction markets give Sims about a 2% chance of winning. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and a wide financial gap — all point in the same direction. Barring an unforeseen development, Williams is positioned to win another term by a comfortable double-digit margin.
